text:
Anya: quick thread — ran a microbenchmark for the sidecar proto fanout + host parse path, saw a consistent p95 latency bump after the kernel-selection change
Sam: oof, how big a bump?
Anya: ~18% p50 and ~32% p95 on small requests (<=64 tokens). end-to-end host parse + tokenize part looks dominant. CPU profile attached below (summarized)
Kevin: can you paste the flame? 
Anya: pasted minimal excerpt:
```
  40.2%  tokenization::utf8_normalize
  18.7%  host::parse::header_unwrap
  12.5%  grpc::writev_flush
   6.9%  kvcache::lookup_serial
   5.0%  kernel_selector::choose_path (fallback->fp32)
```
Sam: interesting — kernel_selector shows fallback to fp32 for some model variants? that 5% + extra mem copies could cascade.
Mira: also saw increased syscall churn on the sidecar, smallwrite pattern. can you share nettrace snippets?
Anya: nettrace shows a lot of small frames (~256B) for 30% of requests — seems proto fanout is splitting streams aggressively. snippet:
```
# grpc write sequence
OUT: header(48) payload(200)
OUT: header(48) payload(120)
OUT: header(48) payload(8)
```
Kevin: that explains grpc::writev_flush hitting more often; writev path not coalescing. small writes + UTF8 normalization cost = bad combo.
Sam: any change to batching heuristics recently? we pushed the new adaptive-batch hinter last week. could interact with kernel selection.
Anya: yes, adaptive-batch changed sequence length bucketting; now many tiny sequences stay uncaptured and stream through host parse. Also kvcache has a higher miss rate for short prefixes — +7% miss.
Mira: so we have three contributors: proto fanout causing microframes, tokenization hotpath cost, and fallback kernel selection. which to tackle first?
Kevin: low-hanging: coalesce small gRPC frames at sidecar level. add a micro-buffer so we don't flush on every tiny fragment.
Sam: agree. patch idea: bump write coalesce threshold from 128B -> 512B for sidecar -> host path, with safety timer 5ms. should reduce syscall rate.
Anya: I already tested locally with that change, p95 dropped ~12% on small RPS. no functional regressions in unit tests.
Mira: second: tokenization micro-optimizations — we can skip full utf8_normalize for ascii-only payloads (fast path). ~25% of requests are ascii-only.
Kevin: third: kernel_selector fallback — we need telemetry to know why fp32 chosen. maybe quantized kernels missing for certain seq lengths or kv-cache state. Add logging: model, seq_len, requested_quant, available_kernels.
perf-bot: perf run queued: job/1812349998-sidecar-coalesce-check (baseline=1812349998). will post results in ~15m. :hourglass: 
deploy-bot: rolling deploy candidate built for sidecar-coalesce (image sha: sha256:deadbeef). canary on 2 hosts when ready.
Sam: timeline: can we land coalesce patch + canary today? then follow with tokenization fastpath early next week and kernel selector telemetry in the same sprint.
Anya: yes. I'll open a PR for coalesce + add the micro-benchmark harness to capture writev counts.
Kevin: one more ask: add a perf counter in kvcache for short-prefix misses (<=8 tokens) so we can correlate with batching changes.
Mira: noted — will add metric: kvcache.short_prefix_miss.rate.
Anya: summary action items:
- Anya: PR for sidecar write coalesce (threshold 512B, timer 5ms) + microbench harness
- Kevin: add kernel_selector telemetry fields to runtime logs
- Mira: add kvcache.short_prefix_miss metric and tokenization ascii fastpath feature flag
- Sam: run canary with deploy-bot once PR builds pass, monitor p50/p95 + writev syscall rate
perf-bot: job completed: sidecar-coalesce-check: 
  result: p95 -11.8% (small-reqs), syscall_rate(write) -42%
Anya: nice — canary going out after CI. tagging folks: @Sam @Kevin @Mira.
Sam: will monitor. thanks all :thumbsup:
Kevin: if we still see kernel fallback after those, we may need a quant kernel fallback table change (follow-up).
Mira: copying to eng-runtime postmortem channel after canary stabilized.
Anya: closing out thread, will link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4822
